beats.script:
HOST: A lot of people on GLP-1s are constipated.
GASTROENTEROLOGIST: Yes.
HOST: Is that okay? I mean, what do people need to do about that?
beats.visual: Open on host above female gastroenterologist, equal halves. Both microphones visible; guest listens, then gives the short answer.
beats.emotion: Podcast · stacked | Overlay: HOW GLP-1s SLOW THE GUT
beats.note:
Start immediately on the question. Hold the split through “Yes” and the follow-up; retain the natural handoff.
REFERENCE FRAMING ONLY — cast our female gastroenterologist; source people and show branding are not final assets.

beats.script: GASTROENTEROLOGIST: So there's a couple of things. The GLP-1 drugs naturally slow down the gut.
beats.visual: Hard cut to guest medium close-up. She gestures naturally as she introduces the two causes.
beats.emotion: Podcast · guest | Overlay: 1 · SLOWER MOVEMENT
beats.note:
Cut on the guest’s answer, matching the reference’s first full-screen guest reveal.
REFERENCE FRAMING ONLY — cast our female gastroenterologist; source people and show branding are not final assets.

beats.script: GASTROENTEROLOGIST: So you get slowed emptying from the stomach
beats.visual: Translucent torso. Isolate stomach and outlet; a small amount of meal contents moves slowly toward the duodenum.
beats.emotion: Science · full frame | Overlay: SLOWER STOMACH EMPTYING
beats.note:
Straight cut on “slowed emptying.” Guest audio continues. No blocked valve or stool in stomach.
EXISTING ASSET PROXY — see planned action; not a newly generated shot.

beats.script: GASTROENTEROLOGIST: and you get slowing of the contractions as well. That can cause constipation.
beats.visual: Return guest large; upper-right inset shows spaced, slower contraction waves along a simplified intestinal segment.
beats.emotion: Podcast + science inset | Overlay: SLOWER CONTRACTIONS
beats.note:
Cut back on “contractions”; keep her conclusion visible. Inset disappears when the thought ends.
REFERENCE FRAMING ONLY — cast our female gastroenterologist; source people and show branding are not final assets.

beats.script: GASTROENTEROLOGIST: The second reason is when you're on a GLP-1, your appetite decreases. And that's one of the benefits that people want.
beats.visual: Guest medium. A small plate icon and a shorter meal indicator appear beside her shoulder as she explains reduced appetite.
beats.emotion: Podcast · guest | Overlay: 2 · SMALLER MEALS

beats.script: GASTROENTEROLOGIST: So you've got the slowing down of the gut, plus you're less hungry and you cut out fiber.

notes.title: Podcast stays central
notes.text: Host on every question. Female guest delivers explanations. Scientific inserts return to her at the conclusion of each thought. Preserve warm cream studio, boom microphones, consistent eyelines and relaxed conversational delivery.

notes.title: Timing and audio
notes.text: 190 delivered words/minute; 0.16s intra-card speaker handoffs; 0.7s end hold. Provisional, not an aligned audio timeline. Final narration 1.1× maximum per user direction; remove dead air first and align cues to actual words. Keep intelligible breaths and short turn-taking pauses. B-roll audio stays muted; speech and continuous room tone bridge cuts. No automatic 1.2× stretch.

notes.title: Caption and overlay system
notes.text: Opening topic strip only during the initial stacked exchange. Then bold white uppercase captions, usually 1–4 words, soft dark shadow, near 60–70% of frame height. Scientific labels stay in the upper third. Keep faces, mouths and bottom platform UI zone unobstructed. Overlays enter on the word they explain.

notes.title: Transitions
notes.text: Hard cuts for speaker changes and B-roll entries/exits. Carry the speaking audio continuously under inserts. Occasional restrained punch-in at a conclusion, approximately 1.08–1.12×. No whip pans, page wipes, noisy whooshes or recurring animated title cards.

notes.title: Scientific direction
notes.text: One clean anatomy style: translucent torso, peach organs, dark teal field, restrained blue for water. Show stomach emptying, intestinal contractions and colon hydration as distinct processes. No stool in stomach, fake studies, product-triggered gut reboot or invented biochemical reactions. Ingredient-role claims remain subject to the evidence limitations in source-notes.md.

notes.title: Casting and future pacing
notes.text: Female gastroenterologist is a casting requirement, not an invented identity. An actual clinician must review and own first-person patient wording. Illustrative lifestyle footage represents desired everyday activities, not documented Motilli outcomes or actual patients.

notes.title: Product source correction
notes.text: The old S27/S28 packshot proxies visibly include stale 5 g / other front-label claims. They are composition references only. Use current approved product artwork for final shots; exactly two green heart-shaped gummies. Verify final physical label reference before media generation.

notes.title: Production routing
notes.text: Storyboard first is the default ad workflow. New stills use GPT Image 2; new video uses Google Omni. Subsequent editing uses the current documented internal editor. Do not start a production timeline from these estimated timecodes; conform after voice and silence cleanup.
